runscript.name: Mi-17 twin-engine FGGearbox validation (one engine inoperative)
runscript.description:
Companion to test_mi17_gearbox_steadystate.xml: starts both aircraft/mi17 engines, lets the shaft settle, then stops engine[1] only (propulsion/engine[1]/set-running=0) to exercise FGGearbox's one-engine-inoperative path -- the actual real-world failure mode a twin-turboshaft helicopter is built to survive, and specifically what makes a genuine two-engines-into-one-rotor model (vs. the single mocked "engine" this config replaced) worth having.
What to check in the notified properties after the engine[1] cutoff event: propulsion/gearbox[0]/one-engine-inoperative should flip to true/1; engine[1]'s output-torque-lbft should decay toward zero (windmilling, no fuel) while engine[0]'s stays substantial (it is now carrying the full shaft load alone); shaft-rpm should sag from its two-engine steady value but must remain positive/finite and settle rather than diverge -- a NaN, negative, or unbounded shaft-rpm here means the gearbox is not handling the asymmetric- input case correctly, not that the aircraft "should" maintain full RPM on one engine (it should not, at these throwaway per-side power tables).

event.name: Two-engine steady-state report (3s, just before cutoff)
